response: The flag of Israel consists of a white background with two horizontal blue stripes and a blue Star of David (also known as the Shield of David) in the center. The blue stripes are positioned near the top and bottom of the flag, dividing the white background into three horizontal sections, with the central section being smaller than the top and bottom sections. The Star of David is a six-pointed star formed by two overlapping triangles and is a symbol of Judaism. The flag's design was inspired by the traditional Jewish prayer shawl, known as a tallit, which also features a blue stripe. The flag was officially adopted on October 28, 1948, shortly after the establishment of the State of Israel.
